mainTopic: For whom may one cook on יום טוב (animals, גויים), hosting a גוי on שבת and יום טוב, and the יום טוב rulings of בית שמאי, בית הלל and רבן גמליאל
overview: The amud opens with a מחלוקת on the word ״לָכֶם״, for you, in the פסוק about cooking on יום טוב. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it excludes animals. רבי עקיבא says it excludes גויים, because you must feed your animals but not גויים. אביי asks how, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, date pits may be thrown to animals. רב יוסף answers that on יום טוב they can be used as fuel, and on שבת they are carried on top of bread. Next the גמרא discusses hosting a גוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids it on יום טוב, in case the host cooks extra for him. רב אחא בר יעקב forbids it even on שבת, because the גוי's leftover wine is איסורי הנאה and so is מוקצה. The final ruling allows it on שבת but not on יום טוב. Then a משנה brings the מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל about heating water and warming oneself by a fire, and the גמרא proves from a ברייתא that the fire ruling follows only בית הלל. A second משנה lists three places where רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי. רב הונא explains that the insulated-food case has no עירובי תבשילין, and his ruling about one loaf and one pot continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: food prep is for you, not for dogs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads ״לָכֶם״ in the פסוק as excluding animals from food-prep מלאכה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For you', and not for dogs. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes the word ״לָכֶם״ from the פסוק about cooking on יום טוב. רבי יוסי הגלילי says this word comes to exclude dogs, meaning animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק permits food-related מלאכה on יום טוב only ״לָכֶם״, for you. רבי יוסי הגלילי takes this as a limit: you may cook for people, but you may not do מלאכה to prepare food for animals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For you', the key word in the פסוק about preparing food on יום טוב
Dogs, standing in for animals in general
תנא who limits יום טוב food prep to people only

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about whether animals may eat on יום טוב. It is about whether you may do a מלאכה, like cooking, specifically for them.

phrases.english: 'For you', and not for dogs,
phrases.notes: From the פסוק אך אשר יאכל לכל נפש הוא לבדו יעשה לכם (שמות יב:טז)

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לָכֶם״ — וְלֹא לִכְלָבִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food-preparation מלאכה on יום טוב is permitted only for people, not for animals.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: animals are included, gentiles are excluded
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says ״כל נפש״ includes animals, and ״לָכֶם״ instead excludes גויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: even the life of an animal is included in the meaning of the פסוק. If so, why does the פסוק say 'for you'? It means for you, and not for גויים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says animals are included, and the word ״לָכֶם״ teaches something else: it excludes גויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says ״לכל נפש״, for every soul. רבי עקיבא reads 'every soul' broadly enough to include animals. He still has to explain the extra limiting word ״לָכֶם״, so he uses it to exclude cooking for גויים.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in the meaning of the words
Why does the פסוק need to say this?

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even the life of an animal is included in the meaning.
phrases.notes: Based on ״לכל נפש״ in the same פסוק

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'for you'?
For you, and not for gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֵמָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same word ״לָכֶם״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food prep on יום טוב is permitted for animals but not for גויים.

steps.title: Why include dogs but exclude gentiles?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason רבי עקיבא has to include animals and exclude גויים, rather than the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you include dogs and exclude גויים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks רבי עקיבא to justify his choice. This sets up the next step, which gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'animals' and 'גויים' could fit under 'every soul' or be cut out by ״לָכֶם״. The question asks for a principle that explains why animals go in and גויים go out, and not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (What is your reason?)

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the dogs
and to exclude the gentiles?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַכְּלָבִים וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי עקיבא's division.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that determines which group is included and which is excluded.

steps.title: Your responsibility to feed is the dividing line
steps.stepSummary: Animals are included because you must feed them. גויים are excluded because you are not responsible for their food.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include dogs, because their food is your responsibility. I exclude גויים, because their food is not your responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The difference is who you are obligated to feed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your own animals depend on you, and you are obligated to feed them. So feeding them counts as a need of yours and fits ״לָכֶם״. גויים are not your obligation, so cooking for them is not 'for you'.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, food prep on יום טוב is allowed for whoever you are responsible to feed. That includes your animals but not גויים.

phrases.english: I include the dogs,
because their food is upon you,
and I exclude the gentiles,
because their food is not upon you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי אֶת הַכְּלָבִים — שֶׁמְּזוֹנוֹתָן עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obligation to feed: you must feed your animals, but not גויים.

steps.title: אביי: how may we throw date pits to animals?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, we may handle date pits on יום טוב to feed animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said 'for you' and not for dogs, how do we throw these date pits to animals on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's view using a common practice. People throw date pits to animals on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Date pits are not human food. If יום טוב permissions are only 'for you', meaning for people, then animal-only food has no permitted use. That would make the pits מוקצה and forbidden to handle, yet people do throw them to animals.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not asking about doing a מלאכה here. Throwing pits is not cooking. His question is about מוקצה, meaning whether you may even handle these pits.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
And according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said 'for you' and not for dogs,
these date pits to animals,
how do we throw them on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוסי הגלילי's view and tests it against practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule that יום טוב permissions are not for animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animal-only food would have no permitted use on יום טוב, so it should be מוקצה. Yet date pits are thrown to animals.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the pits are usable as fuel
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that date pits are not מוקצה because people can use them as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: since they are fit for burning as fuel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. The pits have a human use, as fuel, so they may be handled. Once you may handle them, you may also throw them to animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something is not מוקצה if it has a permitted human use on יום טוב. Burning for cooking is such a use. So the pits are permitted to handle, even according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: He said to him: since they are fit for fuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוֹאִיל וַחֲזוּ לְהַסָּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds an alternative permitted use that removes the מוקצה status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Date pits are only animal food, so they would be מוקצה for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their usefulness as fuel makes them permitted to handle.

steps.title: But moist pits do not burn
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the fuel answer works only for dry pits, not moist ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for dry ones. What is there to say about moist ones?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer. Moist date pits do not burn well, so the fuel reason seems not to apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on the pits being usable as fuel. Wet pits seem useless as fuel, so they should still be מוקצה. Yet people throw them to animals too.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one case)

phrases.english: This works for dry ones;
for moist ones, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּיַבִּישְׁתָּא, בְּרַטִּיבְתָּא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6 by pointing to a case where it does not fit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moist pits cannot serve as fuel, so the fuel reason does not cover them.

steps.title: רב יוסף: moist pits work in a large fire
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that even moist pits are usable fuel in a big fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: they are fit for a large fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his answer. In a large fire, moist pits dry out and then burn, so they still count as fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big fire is strong enough to dry wet pits and then burn them. So moist pits also have a human use and are not מוקצה. רבי יוסי הגלילי's view stands, and the practice of throwing pits to animals is explained.
steps.whatToRemember: Even for רבי יוסי הגלילי, who forbids food-prep מלאכה for animals, date pits may be thrown to animals on יום טוב. This is because they have a human use as fuel, and even moist pits burn in a large fire.

phrases.english: He said to him: they are fit for a large fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזוּ לְהֶיסֵּק גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's follow-up objection about moist pits.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expands the scope of the original answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Moist pits are useless as fuel and therefore מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist pits are usable in a large fire, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: The fuel answer does not work on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that 'usable as fuel' only helps on יום טוב, when lighting a fire is allowed. On שבת, how can the date pits be moved?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works fine on יום טוב. But on שבת, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer again. Burning things is allowed on יום טוב but forbidden on שבת, so 'it's good for fuel' cannot be the reason the pits may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the pits are not מוקצה because they can be burned. But a thing only escapes מוקצה if it has a permitted use on that day. On שבת burning is forbidden, so the pits seem to have no use and should be מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out fine (for this case)
What is there to say? (the answer doesn't cover this case)
An item set aside from use that may not be moved on שבת/יום טוב

phrases.english: That works well on a Festival,
phrases.notes: On יום טוב, lighting a fire for cooking is permitted, so fuel is a real use.

phrases.english: on Shabbat, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: On שבת, burning is forbidden, so the fuel answer fails.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּיוֹם טוֹב, בְּשַׁבָּת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of רב יוסף's fuel answer from steps 6 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that date pits are not מוקצה because they serve as fuel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fuel is only a permitted use on יום טוב. On שבת burning is forbidden, so the pits have no use and should be מוקצה.

steps.title: Carry the pits on top of bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that on שבת the pits are moved together with bread. This follows שמואל, who says a person may use bread for all his needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: We move them along with bread, like שמואל. שמואל said: a person may do all his needs with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new way to move the pits on שבת. You place them on a piece of bread, which may be moved, and carry the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pits stay מוקצה on שבת, but they may be moved indirectly together with a permitted item. Normally using bread as a tray could look like disrespect to food. שמואל rules that this is fine as long as the bread stays edible.

keyTerms.meaning: Along with / on account of (moving one thing together with another)
A person may use bread for any of his needs

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying the pits stop being מוקצה on שבת. They remain מוקצה, and the bread is simply the permitted item that carries them.

phrases.english: We carry them along with bread.
phrases.notes: The pits are placed on bread and moved with it.

phrases.english: In accordance with Shmuel, as Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Source for using bread this way.

phrases.english: A person may perform all his needs with bread.
phrases.notes: Using bread as a tool is not considered disrespect to food, as long as it stays edible.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְטַלְטְלִינַן לְהוּ אַגַּב רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's שבת challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative mechanism: indirect carrying together with a permitted item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On שבת the pits have no use, so there is no way to move them for the animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת the pits may be moved on top of bread, following שמואל's rule that bread may be used for one's needs.
steps.whatToRemember: יום טוב: the pits are usable fuel, so they are not מוקצה. שבת: they are carried along with bread, based on שמואל.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids inviting a גוי on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the earlier lenient ruling about baking extra for a גוי disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי. He allows inviting a גוי on שבת but forbids it on יום טוב, in case the host cooks more for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: you may invite a גוי on שבת, but you may not invite a גוי on יום טוב. This is a גזירה, in case you cook extra for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of cooking for a גוי. It shows that רבי יהושע בן לוי takes a stricter view than the earlier lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת nothing is cooked, so a guest cannot lead to extra cooking. On יום טוב cooking is allowed for Jews, so the host might add food just for the גוי, which is forbidden. That means even a meal made mainly for Jews may not lead to cooking extra for a גוי, which goes against the earlier lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees (this view argues with another)
Lest he cook more for his sake

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the halachic rule about hosting a גוי on יום טוב. It also opens the next discussion about hosting a גוי on שבת.

phrases.english: And it differs from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
phrases.notes: The earlier lenient ruling about baking for a גוי argues with him.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One may invite a gentile on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: No cooking happens on שבת, so there is no risk.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין אֶת הַגּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: but one may not invite a gentile on a Festival,
a decree lest he cook more for his sake.
phrases.notes: Cooking on יום טוב is permitted only for Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the date-pit discussion and returns to cooking for a גוי, showing a disagreement with the earlier lenient ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inviting a גוי is allowed on שבת but forbidden on יום טוב, in case the host cooks extra for him.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב forbids it even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says you may not invite a גוי even on שבת, because of the wine left over in his cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: even on שבת it is also not allowed, because of the leftovers in the cups.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא goes further than רבי יהושע בן לוי. He forbids hosting a גוי even on שבת, for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern here is not cooking. Wine a גוי has touched becomes forbidden, so the leftover in his cup is useless and therefore מוקצה. The host might then move that cup with the forbidden wine on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Even on שבת it is also not allowed

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Even on Shabbat also, no,
phrases.notes: One may not invite a גוי on שבת either.

phrases.english: because of the remnants in the cups.
phrases.notes: The leftover wine is forbidden and useless, so it is מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רבי יהושע בן לוי, forbidding the invitation on שבת too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי may not be invited even on שבת, because the leftover wine in his cup is מוקצה.

steps.title: Then our leftovers should be מוקצה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if leftover wine is useless and מוקצה, then the leftovers in our own cups should be מוקצה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, ours too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב אחא בר יעקב's reasoning. Jews also leave a little wine in their cups, and nobody drinks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'nobody will drink it' made wine מוקצה, every leftover in every cup would be מוקצה. Yet we freely move our own cups on שבת. So the reasoning seems to prove too much.

phrases.english: If so, ours should also be prohibited!
phrases.notes: Our own leftover wine should also be מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דִּידַן נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that leftover wine is מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our own leftovers are also not drunk, yet they are not treated as מוקצה.

steps.title: Our leftovers can feed chickens
steps.stepSummary: The leftovers in our cups are not מוקצה because they can be given to chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ours are fit for chickens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a use for our leftover wine. It can be given to the chickens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something with any permitted use, even for animals, is not מוקצה. Our leftovers have such a use, so they may be moved.

phrases.english: Ours are fit for chickens.
phrases.notes: A use for animals is enough to avoid מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידַן חֲזוּ לְתַרְנְגוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All leftover wine is useless and therefore מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our leftovers can be fed to chickens, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: Their leftovers can feed chickens too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the גוי's leftover wine could also be given to chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Theirs are also fit for chickens!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the distinction just made. Chickens can drink the גוי's leftover wine just as easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If feeding chickens is enough of a use, it should apply to the גוי's leftovers as well. Then they would not be מוקצה, and רב אחא בר יעקב's reason falls away.

phrases.english: Theirs are also fit for chickens!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידְהוּ נָמֵי חֲזוּ לְתַרְנְגוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction that only our leftovers are usable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The chicken use applies equally to the גוי's leftovers.

steps.title: Their leftovers are forbidden for any benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גוי's leftover wine is forbidden for any benefit, so it cannot even be given to chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Theirs are items forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real difference. Wine touched by a גוי is יין נסך, and a Jew may not get any benefit from it, including feeding it to animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding chickens counts as benefit, and benefit from this wine is forbidden. So the גוי's leftovers have no permitted use at all, and they are fully מוקצה. רב אחא בר יעקב's reasoning stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine a גוי has touched, forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: Theirs are items prohibited for benefit.
phrases.notes: Wine touched by a גוי may not be used at all, even for animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידְהוּ אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chicken use applies to both kinds of leftovers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי's wine is איסורי הנאה, so it has no permitted use and is מוקצה.
steps.whatToRemember: Our leftover wine has a use (chickens), so it is not מוקצה. A גוי's leftover wine is איסורי הנאה, so it has no use and is מוקצה.

steps.title: Why not move the wine along with the cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the forbidden wine cannot simply be moved together with the cup. After all, רבא allows moving a coal pan with its ashes even though useless wood pieces are on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him move them along with the cup! Didn't רבא say: you may move a coal pan along with its ashes, even though there are broken pieces of wood on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רב אחא בר יעקב, using a ruling of רבא. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cup is a permitted vessel, so the forbidden leftover wine should be secondary to it and movable along with it. רבא proves this kind of movement is allowed: a coal pan may be moved for its useful ashes even though מוקצה wood bits sit on top. If so, the leftover wine is no reason to forbid hosting a גוי on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't (he) say? Introduces a supporting ruling used to challenge

phrases.english: And let him move them along with the cup?
phrases.notes: The cup is a permitted vessel.

phrases.english: Didn't Rava say:
One may move a coal pan on account of its ashes,
phrases.notes: The ashes are useful, for example to cover dirt.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ שִׁבְרֵי עֵצִים!
phrases.english: even though there are broken pieces of wood on it!
phrases.notes: The wood pieces are מוקצה, yet the pan may be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַלְטְלִינְהוּ אַגַּב כָּסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the leftover wine is מוקצה, challenges whether that actually prevents moving the cup.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's ban on hosting a גוי on שבת because of שיורי כוסות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's ruling, a מוקצה item may be moved along with a permitted one. So the forbidden wine could be moved along with the cup, and there is no problem.

steps.title: Wine forbidden for all benefit is stricter than the wood pieces
steps.stepSummary: The coal-pan case is different, because the wood pieces there are only מוקצה. The גוי's wine is an איסור הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the wood pieces are not forbidden for benefit. Here, the wine is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 17. It explains why רבא's coal-pan ruling does not apply to the גוי's wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wood pieces on the coal pan are merely מוקצה, so they may be carried along with the pan. The גוי's wine is forbidden for any benefit at all. That makes it more serious, so the cup may not be moved just to carry the wine along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Items from which it is forbidden to get any benefit

phrases.english: There, they are not items forbidden for benefit,
phrases.notes: The wood pieces on the coal pan are only מוקצה.

phrases.english: here, they are items forbidden for benefit.
phrases.notes: The גוי's leftover wine (יין נסך).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — לָאו אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the coal-pan challenge by pointing out a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since useless wood may be carried along with a coal pan, the forbidden wine should also be carried along with its cup.
steps.terutzMaskana: Something that is only מוקצה is treated more leniently than something forbidden for all benefit. The wine therefore cannot be carried along with the cup.

steps.title: רב אחא asks to compare the wine to a chamber pot
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי suggests the cup should be removable, just like a disgusting chamber pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of Difti said to רבינא: Let it be like a chamber pot of feces!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי offers a new reason to allow removing the cup. Something disgusting, like a chamber pot, may be taken out of the room on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרף של רעי may be removed on שבת even though it is מוקצה, because it is disgusting to leave it there. Forbidden wine left on the table is also unpleasant. So it should be allowed to clear it away on the same grounds.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא from the town of Difti

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
But let it be like a chamber pot of feces!
phrases.notes: A chamber pot may be removed because it is disgusting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֶהֱוֵי כִּגְרָף שֶׁל רְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the coal-pan comparison was rejected, a different היתר is proposed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the cup with the forbidden wine may not be moved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Disgusting things may be removed on שבת even if they are מוקצה. So the cup with the leftover wine should be removable too.

steps.title: One may not create a chamber-pot situation on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the chamber-pot heter covers a situation that already exists. One may not deliberately set it up in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But may one make a chamber pot in the first place?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אחא. The chamber-pot permission is only for a problem that already happened, not one you create on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a גרף של רעי is a solution after the fact. Someone may not set up a forbidden, disgusting situation just to rely on that היתר. So one should not knowingly cause a גוי's wine to be left in the cup to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: In the first place / from the outset
But may one make? (a rhetorical question meaning 'certainly not')

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying a chamber pot may never be removed. He is saying one may not deliberately create such a situation in order to rely on that permission.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה?
phrases.english: But may one make a chamber pot of feces in the first place?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: certainly not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the chamber-pot comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the היתר (בדיעבד vs. לכתחילה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a chamber pot may be removed, the leftover wine should be removable too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chamber-pot היתר does not allow someone to create such a situation on purpose.

steps.title: מר שמואל's ruling on inviting a גוי on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבא gave מר שמואל permission to teach in public. He taught that one may invite a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, in case the host cooks extra for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא authorized מר שמואל, and he taught: One may invite a גוי on שבת, but one may not invite a גוי on יום טוב. This is a גזירה, in case the host cooks more for his sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on inviting a גוי for a meal. It is fine on שבת, but on יום טוב the חכמים forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, cooking is allowed for Jews but not for a גוי. If a גוי is invited, the host might cook extra food for him. On שבת all cooking is forbidden anyway, so that concern does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: He appointed / authorized him (to teach in public)
And he taught in a public lecture
A protective decree of the חכמים
In case he cooks more for his sake

steps.whatToRemember: Inviting a גוי: allowed on שבת, forbidden on יום טוב, because the host might cook extra for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the practical bottom line for hosting a גוי on these days.

phrases.english: Rava authorized Mar Shmuel, and he taught:
One may invite a gentile on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין אֶת הַגּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: but one may not invite a gentile on a Festival,
a decree, lest he cook more for his sake.
phrases.notes: Cooking on יום טוב is permitted only for Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רָבָא לְמָר שְׁמוּאֵל, וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the practical rule on hosting a גוי after the discussion of his leftover wine.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may invite a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, because of the concern of cooking extra for him.

steps.title: How מרימר and מר זוטרא handled an unexpected guest
steps.stepSummary: When a גוי showed up on יום טוב, מרימר and מר זוטרא told him they would not go to extra trouble for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a גוי happened to come to מרימר and מר זוטרא on יום טוב, they would tell him: If you are happy with what we prepared for ourselves, good. If not, we will not go to extra trouble on your account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how two אמוראים handled a גוי who came without being invited on יום טוב. They let him eat, but made clear they would not cook anything extra for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה is about deliberately inviting a גוי. When he arrives on his own, he may eat what is already prepared. Stating out loud that nothing extra will be cooked removes the worry of שמא ירבה בשבילו.

keyTerms.meaning: On your account / for your sake

phrases.english: Mareimar and Mar Zutra,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מִקְּלַע לְהוּ גּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: when a gentile would happen to come to them on a Festival,
they would say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי נִיחָא לָךְ בְּמַאי דִּטְרִיחָא לַן מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If you are satisfied with what we troubled over for ourselves, good;
and if not, extra trouble
on your account we will not take.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר וּמַר זוּטְרָא, כִּי הֲוָה מִקְּלַע לְהוּ גּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ruling against inviting a גוי on יום טוב worked in practice when a גוי came uninvited.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי who comes uninvited on יום טוב may eat what is already prepared, as long as nothing extra is cooked for him.

steps.title: New משנה: heating water on יום טוב for washing feet
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow heating water on יום טוב for one's feet only if it is also fit to drink. בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: A person may not heat water for his feet unless it is fit for drinking. בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a מחלוקת about heating water on יום טוב for washing one's feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that fire on יום טוב is allowed only for food-related needs. So the water must at least be drinkable. בית הלל permit heating it even just for washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Even according to בית שמאי, heating water is not completely forbidden. It is allowed if the water is also fit to drink.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
A person may not heat water for his feet
unless it is fit for drinking.
But Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: a new משנה begins after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: water heated for the feet must be drinkable. בית הלל: heating it is permitted even just for washing.

steps.title: Making a fire to warm oneself on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may make a fire on יום טוב and warm himself by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may make a fire and warm himself facing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second ruling. It permits lighting a bonfire on יום טוב for warmth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Warming oneself is not food preparation; it is a benefit to the whole body. The next step asks whether בית שמאי agree to this ruling, and step 26 shows that it is only בית הלל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Facing it / in front of it

phrases.english: A person may make a fire
and warm himself facing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם מְדוּרָה וּמִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגְדָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further ruling in the same משנה about using fire on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may make a fire on יום טוב in order to warm oneself.

steps.title: Who taught the fire ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's היתר to warm oneself by a fire on יום טוב is accepted even by בית שמאי, or only by בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: this ruling about a fire, who taught it? Is it everyone's view, and בית שמאי see a difference between enjoying with your whole body and enjoying with one limb? Or maybe בית הלל taught it, and בית שמאי see no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who stands behind the משנה's ruling that one may make a fire on יום טוב and warm himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, בית שמאי forbade heating water for one's feet unless it was also fit to drink. So the question is whether בית שמאי would still allow warming the whole body by a fire, because whole-body benefit is more like the basic need of eating. Or perhaps בית שמאי forbid both cases, and the משנה is only בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a dilemma)
A bonfire / fire made for warmth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think בית שמאי forbid all fire on יום טוב. They allow cooking food. The only question is whether warming the body counts like that basic need.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
This ruling about a fire, who taught it?
Is it everyone's opinion,
and Beit Shammai see a difference

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הֲנָאַת כׇּל גּוּפוֹ לַהֲנָאַת אֵבֶר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: between benefit of the whole body and benefit of one limb,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps Beit Hillel taught it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לָא שָׁנֵי לְהוּ?
phrases.english: but Beit Shammai see no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הַאי מְדוּרָה מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who holds the משנה ruling quoted in step 24, given the מחלוקת in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית שמאי agree to warming oneself by a fire on יום טוב, because of the whole-body vs. one-limb distinction.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the fire ruling is only בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states openly that בית שמאי forbid making a fire to warm oneself, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בית שמאי say a person may not make a fire and warm himself by it. בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that shows בית שמאי forbid warming oneself by a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית שמאי openly forbid it, they do not distinguish between the whole body and one limb. So the משנה's היתר follows בית הלל alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source that answers the question)

steps.whatToRemember: Warming oneself by a fire on יום טוב is a מחלוקת. בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל permit it. The משנה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם מְדוּרָה וְיִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגְדָּהּ.
phrases.english: A person may not make a fire and warm himself by it.
And Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows בית הלל only. בית שמאי forbid warming oneself by a fire.

steps.title: Three cases where רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists three rulings where רבן גמליאל followed בית שמאי's strict view: insulating hot food, setting up a candelabrum, and baking thick loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: In three things רבן גמליאל is strict like בית שמאי: one may not insulate hot food from the start on יום טוב, one may not set up a candelabrum on יום טוב, and one may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three יום טוב rules where רבן גמליאל was strict, following בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, insulating hot food on יום טוב for שבת must be done before יום טוב. Second, a fallen metal candelabrum may not be stood back up, since it looks like building. Third, only thin loaves may be baked, since thick loaves take much more effort.

keyTerms.meaning: Insulating hot food to keep it warm
From the outset; in the first place

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three things

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַחְמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel is strict like the words of Beit Shammai:
One may not insulate hot food
from the outset on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and one may not stand up the candelabrum on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
phrases.english: and one may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַחְמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל forbids insulating hot food from the start on יום טוב, standing up a candelabrum, and baking thick loaves.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל cites his family's practice
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל supports the thick-loaves rule by saying his father's household never baked thick loaves on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: in all the days of my father's house, they never baked thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל brings support for his strict ruling on thick loaves from the custom of his own family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses real-life practice in a great household as evidence for the law. The next line will question whether that practice proves anything.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
In all the days of my father's household

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
phrases.english: they did not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third ruling of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on baking thick loaves on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבן גמליאל's father's household.

steps.title: The חכמים: your family was strict only on itself
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. His father's household was strict on itself but ruled leniently for all of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: what can we do about your father's house? They were strict on themselves, but lenient for all of Israel, letting them bake thick loaves and coal-baked cakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבן גמליאל's proof from his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A personal stringency is not the same as the law. His family ruled for the public that thick loaves and חררין are allowed. So their private custom proves nothing about what is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: A great person's personal stringency does not set the law for everyone. The public ruling of רבן גמליאל's family was lenient.

phrases.english: They said to him:
What shall we do about your father's household,
who were strict on themselves
and lenient for all of Israel,
to bake thick loaves and coal-baked cakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה נַעֲשֶׂה לְבֵית אָבִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the family-practice proof for the thick-loaves ban.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The family's practice was a personal stringency. Their ruling for the public was lenient.

steps.title: What case is the insulating-food ruling about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the hot-food case. If an עירובי תבשילין was made, why do בית שמאי forbid? If not, why do בית הלל permit?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he set aside an עירובי תבשילין, what is בית שמאי's reason? And if he did not set aside an עירובי תבשילין, what is בית הלל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case of the first ruling, insulating hot food on יום טוב for שבת. It shows that either way, one side seems hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an עירובי תבשילין, preparing on יום טוב for שבת is allowed, so בית שמאי's ban makes no sense. Without one, all preparing for שבת should be forbidden, so בית הלל's היתר makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
The food set aside before יום טוב that lets one cook on יום טוב for Shabbat

steps.confusionAlert: The hot food here is being insulated on יום טוב for the שבת that falls right after it. That is why עירובי תבשילין comes up.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the case?
If he set aside an eiruv tavshilin,
what is the reason of Beit Shammai?
And if he did not set aside an eiruv tavshilin,
what is the reason of Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּאַנַּח עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first ruling of the משנה in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מחלוקת about insulating hot food on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases fail. With an עירוב, בית שמאי's ban is unexplained. Without one, בית הלל's heter is unexplained.

steps.title: רב הונא: no עירוב, but enough to live on is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the case is with no עירובי תבשילין. Still, according to בית הלל, the רבנן allowed a person to prepare what he needs for basic living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: really, I will tell you the case is where he did not set aside an עירובי תבשילין. Even so, the רבנן allowed him enough for his basic needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by choosing the second case, no עירוב, and explaining בית הלל's היתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, one may not cook fully for שבת. But בית הלל hold that the רבנן allowed the bare minimum a person needs to live, such as one hot dish. בית שמאי do not allow even that.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I will tell you (answer that keeps one side of a dilemma)

steps.whatToRemember: The case of insulating hot food has no עירובי תבשילין. בית הלל allow it as basic sustenance (כדי חייו). בית שמאי and רבן גמליאל forbid it.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Actually, I will tell you
that he did not set aside an eiruv tavshilin,
and the Sages permitted him enough for his sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case and adds a sustenance heter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an עירוב, nothing at all may be prepared for שבת, so בית הלל cannot be explained.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without an עירוב, בית הלל still allow the bare minimum needed to live. בית שמאי forbid even that.

steps.title: רב הונא is consistent: one loaf and one pot are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב הונא's answer about insulating hot food fits his own known ruling. Even without an עירובי תבשילין, a person may have one loaf baked and one pot cooked for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא follows his own reasoning, as רב הונא said: someone who did not set up an עירובי תבשילין, they bake one loaf for him and cook one pot for him,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up רב הונא's previous answer by quoting another ruling of his that says the same thing. The quote is not finished yet and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, רב הונא said that even without an עירובי תבשילין, a person may prepare what he needs for basic living. Here we see where that idea comes from: his rule that a person with no עירובי תבשילין still gets one loaf and one pot. So his answer was not made up for that one case. It follows a principle he holds in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his known view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as permission to cook freely without an עירובי תבשילין. The allowance is only a minimum (one loaf and one pot) so the person is not left without basic food for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that someone who forgot to make an עירובי תבשילין is still allowed a minimal amount of preparation for שבת.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna follows his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: Signals that the previous answer is consistent with his other rulings.

phrases.english: as Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: Introduces the supporting ruling.

phrases.english: one who did not prepare an eiruv tavshilin —
phrases.notes: On the eve of a יום טוב that falls before שבת.

phrases.english: they may bake one loaf for him,
phrases.notes: Basic bread for שבת.

phrases.english: and cook one pot for him,
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב הונא's answer in step 31 matches another ruling of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without an עירובי תבשילין, a person may still have one loaf baked and one pot cooked for him (the list continues).
